identity_held_roles.title: IT Director of Quality Assurance
identity_held_roles.description:
**ABOUT ETHOS & THE OPPORTUNITY**

Ethos Risk Services is a leading insurance claims investigation and medical management company focused on delivering better data, technology, and insights that help our clients make better decisions. We are continuing to invest in our technology organization and are seeking an experienced engineering leader to help scale how software is built, tested, and delivered.

We are seeking a **full-time Director of Quality Assurance** to own software quality across Ethos, overseeing an outsourced QA team and the processes, tooling, environments, and metrics that prevent defects from reaching production. Our ideal candidate is an experienced, results-driven QA leader who will establish a consistent defect lifecycle, reduce defect aging, implement effective root cause analysis and preventive measures, and improve the reliability of test environments. Within their first year, they will standardize QA tools and processes, integrate AI-based solutions into daily QA operations and performance tracking, and establish a comprehensive KPI framework that drives measurable improvements in software quality, efficiency, and accountability.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

* **Lead Outsourced QA Operations:** Direct the day-to-day activities of an outsourced QA team of 8 to10 resources, establishing priorities, performance expectations, and accountability for quality deliverables.
* **Manage Vendor Performance:** Oversee vendor agreements, SLAs, staffing, onboarding, and performance evaluations. Address performance gaps through corrective action and ensure effective knowledge transfer and documentation.
* **Drive Defect Management:** Establish and enforce standardized defect tracking, classification, prioritization, and resolution processes. Lead regular defect triage with engineering and product teams to manage backlogs and identify quality risks.
* **Prevent Production Issues:** Lead structured root cause analysis of production defects, identify recurring failure patterns, and implement preventive measures through improved test coverage, regression testing, and quality gates.
* **Oversee Test Environments:** Partner with DevOps to maintain stable, production-representative QA, staging, and UAT environments, including configuration standards, test data management, and environment availability.
* **Define QA Strategy & Standards:** Develop and continuously improve QA processes across manual, automated, regression, integration, performance, and user acceptance testing to strengthen quality and consistency.
* **Advance Test Automation:** Evaluate and implement QA tools and automation frameworks, integrating automated testing into CI/CD pipelines to improve testing efficiency, coverage, and release reliability.
* **Leverage AI-Enabled QA Tools:** Apply AI-based solutions to test generation, defect classification, failure analysis, workload management, and performance monitoring. Evaluate emerging tools and implement solutions that deliver measurable improvements while maintaining appropriate security and accuracy controls.
* **Establish Quality KPIs:** Define and monitor performance metrics, including defect escape rates, resolution times, automation coverage, recurring production incidents, test effectiveness, and vendor SLA adherence.
* **Deliver Executive Reporting:** Produce monthly quality reports and quarterly reviews for the VP of Engineering and CTO, translating performance data into actionable insights, risks, trends, and recommendations.
* **Support Release Readiness:** Collaborate with engineering, DevOps, IT Delivery Leads, and Technical Product Owners to integrate QA into sprint and release planning, assess release quality, and recommend readiness for deployment.

**QUALIFICATIONS**

**Education:** Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, or equivalent practical experience (required).

**Required Experience:**

* 8 to 10 years of progressively greater responsibility in software quality assurance.
* 3 to 4 years in a QA management role leading teams and managers.
* Proven expertise in defect lifecycle management, root cause analysis, and preventive quality practices.
* Hands-on experience establishing and maintaining test environments and test data management practices.
* Strong working knowledge of QA tooling, such as test management (e.g., Xray, Zephyr, TestRail), defect tracking (e.g., Jira, Azure DevOps), and automation frameworks (e.g., Selenium, Playwright, Cypress).
* Practical experience using AI-based tools in QA or team management, and enthusiasm for expanding their use.
* Experience defining QA KPIs and producing executive-level monthly and quarterly reporting.
* Familiarity with CI/CD pipelines and integrating automated testing into delivery workflows.

**Preferred Experience:**

* Performance, security, or API testing, and a regulated-industry background.
* Certifications: ISTQB Advanced or Test Manager, CSQE, or similar.
* Experience with data visualization or dashboard tools (e.g., Power BI, Tableau)

**WORKING AT ETHOS**

This is a 100% remote U.S.-based role, offering the flexibility to work from home while remaining closely connected to a collaborative leadership team. Our ideal candidate is available during EST standard business hours. Occasional travel may be required for quarterly or annual leadership meetings and company events.

**Candidates must be authorized to work in the United States and must not require current or future employment sponsorship.**

**Benefits include:** Paid Time Off and Sick Time **|** Medical, Dental, and Vision Insurance **|** Short-Term + Long-Term Disability Insurance + Life Insurance **|** 401(k) Matching **|** Employee Referral Bonus Program

At Ethos, you'll have the opportunity to make a meaningful impact, shape the future of our engineering organization, and help build the systems and processes that support our next stage of growth. **To learn more about Ethos, visit our website:** https://ethosrisk.com/about-us/

*Ethos Risk Services is an equal opportunity employer and considers qualified applicants without regard to any characteristic protected by applicable law.*

identity_held_roles.title: VP of Production
identity_held_roles.description:
**VP of Production**
--------------------

**Location:** Los Angeles, Detroit, or San Francisco 
**Employment:** Full time, in person 
**Base salary:** $200,000–$350,000 annually

American factories deserve a supply chain that moves as fast as they do. Nox Metals is building it, along with the tools that run it. We’re a technology company supplying raw metal to frontier American manufacturers. We use software and automation to supply metal to factories faster than the industry thought possible.

### **The role**

We’re hiring a VP of Production to lead manufacturing performance across Nox Metals’ facilities. You will own how work moves through our factories: production planning, daily execution, capacity, staffing, quality, productivity, and on-time delivery.

This is a hands-on manufacturing leadership role with real time on the factory floor. You will develop production leaders, resolve constraints, and create repeatable ways of working that help teams deliver as demand grows. Success means safe, reliable production and clear accountability from the daily schedule through completed customer orders.

### **You will**

* Lead production execution across facilities, with clear expectations for safety, quality, output, cost, and delivery.
* Translate demand into practical production, staffing, shift, and capacity plans.
* Develop plant and production leaders who take ownership of results and build strong teams.
* Establish daily operating reviews, shift handoffs, escalation paths, and performance measures that drive action.
* Identify bottlenecks, reduce downtime and rework, and improve material flow and labor productivity.
* Build consistent training, work instructions, and qualification standards while staying close to how work happens.
* Protect material traceability and quality throughout production.
* Partner with maintenance and engineering on equipment reliability, capacity improvements, and automation.
* Work with supply chain and commercial teams to align material availability, production commitments, and customer needs.
* Partner with finance on production economics and equipment investment decisions.
* Help new or expanded facilities establish reliable production and sustain performance as they ramp.

### **You are**

* A manufacturing leader with a record of improving factory performance and developing accountable leaders.
* Experienced managing production teams, schedules, equipment constraints, and competing priorities.
* Uncompromising about safety, quality, and traceability.
* Fluent in capacity, throughput, labor productivity, downtime, and delivery performance.
* Comfortable making decisions on the floor and following through until problems are resolved.
* Practical, direct, and interested in improving manufacturing with software and automation.

identity_held_roles.title: Director of Operations
identity_held_roles.description:
Karman Space & Defense is a leader in the rapid design, development, and production of critical, next-generation system solutions that align with the U.S. Department of War and its allies' core mission priorities, and meet the accelerating demand for access to space. Building on nearly 50 years of success, we deliver Payload & Protection Systems, Aero/Hydrodynamic Interstage Systems, and Propulsion & Launch Systems to more than 80 prime contractors supporting over 130 space and defense programs.

This role is part of our Space and Launch business, which has contributed to the nation's space programs for decades by delivering complete solutions from concept to flight. We enable successful space operations with mission-critical technology supporting every step from first launch to final landing, including launch vehicle subsystems, propulsion systems, aerodynamic and interstage systems, and payload protection and deployment. Our high-performance solutions are engineered to operate in the most extreme environments and meet precise mission requirements.

Lead manufacturing operations across Karman's El Monte and Corona locations, aligning machining, fabrication, and downstream processing with business objectives. In this role, you will drive safety, quality, delivery, cost, productivity, and profitability by providing operational leadership, strengthening cross-functional collaboration, and advancing continuous improvement initiatives across complex manufacturing environments.

**Responsibilities**

* Leads and coordinates manufacturing operations across the El Monte and Corona locations, establishing accountability, performance expectations, and operating rhythms for operations managers and functional departments.
* Develops and executes operational plans that align production performance, capacity, and investment priorities with company strategy.
* Oversees machining, fabrication, forming, finishing, and assembly operations to improve throughput, schedule attainment, labor productivity, and profitability.
* Drives operational excellence by implementing procedures and standards that improve safety, quality, delivery, cost, and regulatory compliance.
* Champions Lean manufacturing and continuous improvement through 5S, Kaizen, flow and lead-time improvements, cycle-time and setup reduction, Total Productive Maintenance (TPM), and preventative maintenance.
* Analyzes financial and production data, including overall equipment effectiveness (OEE), spindle utilization, and labor efficiency, to manage budgets, inventory, spending, and cost performance.
* Ensures equipment readiness, maintenance execution, and manufacturing capacity align with production requirements.
* Partners with human resources on workforce planning, recruiting, organizational structure, labor utilization, work scheduling, leadership development, performance evaluation, and succession planning.
* Coordinates closed-loop communication and escalation across operations, engineering, quality, supply chain, and program management.
* Manages the administration and performance of subcontracted and temporary labor services.

**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in engineering, operations management, manufacturing, or a related technical discipline, or an equivalent combination of education and experience that includes a minimum of 10 years of relevant manufacturing leadership experience.
* At least 10 years of progressive manufacturing leadership experience, including oversight of complex production environments.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Master of Business Administration (MBA), Master of Science (MS), or another advanced degree.
* Operational leadership experience in precision manufacturing supporting aerospace or defense production.
* Leadership experience in a computer numerical control (CNC) machining environment producing large, tight-tolerance metallic components.
* Experience machining aluminum using 3-axis and 5-axis milling and large gantry equipment.
* Experience with automated or semi-automated manufacturing equipment.
* Experience managing multi-step manufacturing routings and complex production flows.
* Working knowledge of deburring, finishing, forming, welding coordination, heat treatment, and assembly operations.
* Experience building high-performance manufacturing teams and leading Lean transformation.

**Physical Requirements**

* Frequently sits, uses a computer, and communicates.
* Occasionally stands, walks, reaches, or stoops.
* Uses close vision and works with screens for extended periods.
* The essential functions of this position must be performed with or without reasonable accommodation.

This position requires U.S. person status under U.S. export control laws, including U.S. citizens and nationals, lawful permanent residents, refugees, and asylees.

**Benefits**

* Medical, dental, and vision insurance
* 401(k) with company match
* Paid time off
* Health Savings Account (HSA) with company contribution
* Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA)
* Company‑paid life and AD&D insurance
* Short‑ and long‑term disability coverage
* Tuition reimbursement

Karman Space and Defense is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, protected veteran status, or any other status protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.

identity_held_roles.title: Director Quality & Compliance
identity_held_roles.description:
**Job Description:**

**Who We Are:**

At Cart.com, we're **defining the future of commerce.**

Founded to solve the growing complexity of modern commerce, Cart.com helps businesses simplify how they sell, fulfill, and deliver products to their customers. We bring together technology, services, and logistics infrastructure into one connected platform, making it easier for organizations to grow, operate efficiently, and navigate an increasingly fragmented commerce landscape.

We work with brands, retailers, manufacturers, and public sector organizations to support every stage of the customer journey, from ecommerce and order management to fulfillment, distribution, and delivery. By combining software, expertise, and a nationwide logistics network into a unified solution, we help our customers move faster, operate smarter, and scale with confidence.

But what truly sets Cart.com apart is our people. We're builders, problem-solvers, and innovators who thrive on turning big challenges into meaningful outcomes for our customers. Every day, we're helping shape the future of commerce while creating opportunities to learn, grow, and make an impact.

If you're energized by solving complex problems, collaborating with talented teammates, and helping build what's next, we'd love to hear from you.

**Cart.com Milestones**

* Founded in 2020 with a vision to build the first truly unified commerce platform.
* Achieved unicorn status with a valuation exceeding $1 billion.
* Raised more than $475 million to support continued growth and innovation
* Expanded a nationwide commerce and logistics network that helps organizations scale, fulfill, and grow across channels.
* Recognized by Inc.'s Power Partner Awards for helping businesses grow and scale.
* Recognized as an award-winning employer for four consecutive years, reflecting our commitment to building an environment where talented people can grow, innovate, and make an impact.

**Our values:** Cart.com is building a company that is committed to living out these 6 core values:

* **Be brand obsessed:** Our lives are shaped by the brands we interact with daily. We obsess over the brands we serve, and about the things they care about.
* **Think beyond the box:** “We’ve always done it that way” is not a phrase uttered often at our office. We create creative solutions to complex problems.

* **Don’t give up:** We learn from our challenges and see them for what they are; great building blocks to an amazing brand story.
* **Speak up:** We communicate clearly and directly because we care deeply. Communication is the bedrock of our community.
* **Work together:** We’ve built a team that prides itself on diversity of thought and background. Collaboration is better with contrast.
* **Remember to be human:** We work hard, but we leave room for the people, places and things that we love

**AI is part of how we work. It's not doing the hiring.** 
 
We'll use AI in parts of our process and we think you should feel free to use it too — for research, prep, whatever helps. But our interviews exist to meet *you*, not your best AI-assisted draft. Real people make every call here. Any questions about how this works, just ask.

**Remote:**

This position is fully remote and open to candidates in AZ, CA, CO, CT, DC, DE, FL, GA, HI, IL, IN, KY, LA, MA, MD, MI, MO, MS, NC, NJ, NY, NC, OH, OR, PA, SC, TN, TX, UT, VA, WA. The salary range for this role is $175,000-200,000 annually. Actual compensation may vary based on geographic location, experience and qualifications. This role is eligible for bonus, equity and benefits including medical, dental, vision, 401(k), paid time off. Applications accepted through 1-31-2027. We comply with all applicable pay transparency laws in the states where we operate.

**The Role:**

The Director, Quality and Compliance leads the quality function for Cart.com’s federal pharmaceutical distribution business across four sites. This leader will standardize and strengthen an established quality program, develop site quality leaders, ensure consistent application of procedures, and serve as the primary quality point of contact for client reporting, audits and product-quality events.

This is approximately a 70% strategic leadership and 30% hands-on role. The Director will not build the program from the ground up, but will assess the current-state program, make targeted improvements, and ensure teams consistently execute against client, regulatory and network requirements. The role is remote with approximately 30% travel.

**What You’ll Do**

* Lead and develop site quality leaders across Maryland, Goodyear, Temecula and Memphis, establishing clear accountability, delegation and follow-through.
* Standardize quality procedures and expectations across the network while refining the existing quality management system and closing identified gaps.
* Ensure sites remain prepared for client and regulatory audits; support audit planning, host or coordinate inspections, and oversee timely responses and corrective actions.
* Serve as the primary quality point of contact for pharmaceutical product excursions and related client reporting, ensuring submissions are accurate, complete and timely.
* Oversee quality processes supporting receiving, quarantine, release, disposition, returns, destruction, recalls, deviations, corrective and preventive actions, change control, training, complaints and document control.
* Guide quality decisions for controlled-temperature pharmaceutical products, including refrigerated, frozen and ultra-cold storage and distribution.
* Partner with site Operations leaders and Cart.com’s Compliance team to implement operational changes required to meet quality standards and client expectations.
* Use quality metrics, audit findings, client feedback and site observations to identify risk, prioritize improvements and report progress to senior leadership.
* Travel to sites for audit preparation, team development, quality reviews and issue resolution.

**Who You Are:**

 

* You are a strategic, hands-on quality leader who can set direction while stepping into audits, excursions and site-readiness work when needed.
* You lead through others, delegate clearly, establish checkpoints and hold site quality leaders accountable for follow-through.
* You put the client’s requirements first, ask the right questions and respond with accurate, timely information.
* You communicate with credibility and composure across clients, regulators, Operations, Compliance and senior leadership.
* You are highly organized and disciplined, ensuring commitments, documentation and escalations do not get lost.
* You build strong cross-functional partnerships and can influence operational changes without creating a separate quality silo.
* You adapt to changing federal-client requirements while maintaining consistent quality standards and sound judgment.
* You develop people, address performance gaps directly and create a culture of ownership across a distributed team.

**What You’ve Done:**

 

* 7+ years of progressive pharmaceutical quality experience, including work in a current Good Manufacturing Practice (cGMP) environment.
* 5+ years of people-leadership experience with demonstrated success delegating, developing leaders and holding teams accountable. Direct leadership of quality teams is preferred.
* Worked in pharmaceutical distribution, wholesale, logistics or third-party logistics (3PL). Manufacturing experience alone is not sufficient without meaningful distribution-quality exposure.
* Applied cGMP, Good Distribution Practice (GDP), controlled-document and standard operating procedure requirements in a regulated pharmaceutical environment.
* Prepared for or led audits involving the U.S. Food and Drug Administration or comparable regulators, including managing responses and follow-up actions.
* Supported pharmaceutical product release, disposition, holds, recalls or temperature-excursion decisions in a regulated distribution setting.
* Written, revised or implemented quality procedures and documentation, then ensured consistent execution across teams or sites.
* Led a distributed or multi-site team and built accountability through site leaders rather than personally owning every task.
* Managed a significant client, product-quality or regulatory issue requiring coordination across Quality, Operations and Compliance.
* Earned a bachelor’s degree in life sciences, pharmacy, biology, chemistry or a related field, or bring an equivalent combination of relevant education and experience.
* Ability to travel up to 30%.

**Nice to Haves:**

 

* Background supporting federal health programs or agencies such as HHS, DLA, ASPR, BARDA, DoD or VA.
* Experience with pharmaceutical 3PLs, wholesalers, state licensing or NABP accreditation.
* Hands-on experience with vaccines or other cold-chain and ultra-cold pharmaceutical products.
* Knowledge of Drug Supply Chain Security Act requirements and suspect or illegitimate product processes.
* Relevant certifications such as ASQ Certified Quality Auditor, Certified Manager of Quality/Organizational Excellence, Certified Pharmaceutical GMP Professional or Lead Auditor.
* Master’s degree in a life-sciences or related discipline.

**Physical Demands & Working Conditions:**

 

* Remote work environment with regular computer and video-conference use.
* Ability to travel by air or ground up to 30% and work onsite in warehouse, pharmaceutical distribution and temperature-controlled environments.
* Ability to move through operating areas and wear required personal protective equipment when visiting sites.
* Flexibility to support audits, client needs or quality events outside standard business hours when required.

Eligibility Requirement: This position is open only to U.S. citizens due to applicable federal requirements. By applying, you confirm that you are a U.S. citizen and can provide acceptable documentation verifying your status if selected. 
 
If you are not a U.S. citizen, please do not apply for this role.

Cart.com is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

identity_held_roles.description:
**Description**

Sanmina Corporation (Nasdaq: SANM) is a global powerhouse in integrated manufacturing solutions serving the fastest growing segments of the global Electronics Manufacturing Services (EMS) market. We are a global engine providing the end-to-end manufacturing backbone for the world's most essential and innovative brands. Whether it's autonomous vehicles, life-saving medical tech, next-gen aerospace, or AI/cloud infrastructure - our integrated solutions don’t just meet standards—they redefine them.Sanmina Corporation (Nasdaq: SANM) is a leading integrated manufacturing solutions provider serving the fastest-growing segments of the global Electronics Manufacturing Services (EMS) market. Job Purpose:As Quality Director the role will be responsible for developing a world class quality culture and drive region wide continuous improvement projects that result in unparalleled quality performance. You will have the opportunity to reinforce foundational quality principles, as we develop innovative manufacturing, test, inspection and automation processes to build high quality semiconductor, defense and data infrastructure products. This position will be responsible for managing, coordinating and administering all functions of the region’s Quality Management System.What You'll DoLead and mentor QA organizations.Be an outspoken advocate for Quality First throughout the regionExpediently and effectively communicate with customers on quality escapes, visits, escalations, etc.Help maintain and improve the site QMS (including NCR and CAPA system, internal audit, training, etc.)Responsible for ensuring effective quality planning (including PFMEAs, process flows and control plans) for NPI and production parts.Help maintain the site QMS compliance with ISO 9001:2015 and TL9000, ISO 13485, FDA registration and any other regulatory compliance in line with the factory center of excellence Act as advisory to developing additional sources of data and tracking and reporting key Quality-related performance indicators (KPIs), including first pass yield, scrap rates and statistical process control.Oversight of managing and improving site supplier qualityBe an advocate for lean and six sigma manufacturing principles and drive continuous improvementDrive cross functional projects with manufacturing, supply chain, and engineering to verify and validate existing manufacturing processes and capabilitiesCoordinate development of Quality Plan and participate in Design for Manufacturability (DFM) reviews for new customer on-boardingAddress process yields by driving cross-functional teams to develop and implement corrective actions utilizing a methodical approach (DMAIC) to root cause and continuous improvement. What You'll BringBachelor’s Degree required, Mechanical, Aerospace, Industrial or Mfg Engineering preferred10+ years of Quality Engineering or Management experience in a regulated manufacturing environment. Printed circuit board experience is a plus but not required5+ years of direct people managementKnowledge of IPC-6012 and IPC-A-600 desiredDemonstrated experience working directly with customers to resolve concerns, conduct audits and host visitsUnderstanding of ISO 9001:2015, AS9100, TL-9000, ISO-14385, ISO-14001, MIL-PRF-31032 or similar standards with demonstrated success in passing certification auditsExpert level knowledge of root cause analysis techniques and corrective actionHands on experience working with suppliers to improve qualityKnowledge of lean principles (Green or Black belt certification a plus)Knowledge and experience in the application of statistical process controlDemonstrated experience leading diverse teams in a dynamic environment requiredExcellent written and verbal communication and presentation skills requiredOpen-minded self-starter with the ability to adapt, improvise and problem solve, as well manage multiple tasks and projects and concisely explain complex issues supported with data.Excellent analytical abilities and comprehensive understanding of quality toolbox (SPC, 8D, FMEA, Control Plans, etc.) Salary Range (annual): $140,000 - $165,000 Why Join Us?At Sanmina, base pay is one part of our total compensation package and is determined within a range. This provides the opportunity to progress as you grow and develop within a role. The base pay range for this role is between $xx and $xx, and your base pay will depend on your skills, qualifications, experience, and location.Sanmina employees also receive benefits including: Comprehensive medical and dental coverage, retirement benefits, and for formal education related to advancing your career at Sanmina, reimbursement for certain educational expenses — including tuition. Additionally, this role might be eligible for discretionary bonuses or commission payments as well as relocation.Sanmina is an Equal Opportunity Employer and prohibits discrimination and harassment. Sanmina provides equal employment opportunities to employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local laws.Please be aware that this position may require access to technology, software, or technical data that is subject to U.S. export control laws. All offers of employment are contingent on the applicant either 1) being a "U.S. Person," defined as a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful permanent resident, or (iii) other protected individual, such as a refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157 or asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158; or 2) being eligible to obtain a timely export control license or license exception from the applicable U.S. federal agency.

existing_roles.title: Director, Quality Performance Operations
existing_roles.description:
**Company****:**
================

AHI agilon health, inc.

**Job Posting Location****:**
=============================

Remote - USA

**Job Title****:**
==================

Director, Quality Performance Operations

**Job Description****:**
========================

***Candidates must be legally authorized to work in the United States without employer sponsorship, now or in the future.***

The Director, Quality Operations is a hands-on, results-driven operator responsible for disciplined, scalable execution across HEDIS, Stars, clinical quality programs, and the In-Home Assessment (IHA) program. Reporting to the Senior Director, Quality, this role provides operational leadership for the Quality Operations team and directly oversees the Senior Program Manager, Quality Operations. The Director serves as the critical connection point between the centralized operations team and regional and market teams, between operations and technology, and alongside the Payor team with our health plan partners, ensuring priorities are clear, commitments are tracked, and work gets done. This role is built for a strong operator with a bias for action: someone who brings structure to complexity, holds teams and partners accountable, closes loops, and consistently delivers measurable improvement in quality results.

**Essential Job Function**s:

**1. Operational Leadership and Execution**

Lead the day-to-day operating model for enterprise quality programs, including HEDIS, Stars, ACO/MSSP quality initiatives, clinical quality programs, and the IHA program.

Execute priorities set by the Senior Director through annual operating plans, workstreams, milestones, accountabilities, and measurable outcomes.

Directly manage and develop the Senior Program Manager, Quality Operations, and provide leadership across the broader quality operations team.

Serve as the primary liaison between the centralized Quality Operations team and regional and market teams, ensuring enterprise priorities, workflows, and expectations are clearly communicated, adopted, and executed locally, and that market needs, barriers, and feedback are surfaced and resolved centrally.

Establish and run a disciplined operating cadence, including action-item tracking, issue logs, escalation paths, and KPI scorecards, so that commitments are owned, deadlines are met, and open items are driven to closure.

**2. IHA Program Oversig**ht

Own end-to-end operational oversight of the IHA program, including implementation planning, workflow design, market readiness, vendor coordination, KPI monitoring, and issue resolution.

Partner with market, clinical, analytics, coding, risk adjustment, and health plan teams to ensure IHA activities support quality and clinical objectives.

Monitor IHA program productivity, completion, quality, member experience, documentation, and downstream outcomes; implement corrective actions when results are below target.

Drive consistent IHA execution across regions and markets, holding vendors and internal partners accountable to targets and ensuring identified gaps and follow-up needs are closed.

**3. Quality Program Operation**s

Ensure operational readiness for HEDIS/Stars submissions, audits, roadmaps and health plan deliverables.

Coordinate enterprise and market-level quality calendars, dependencies, risks, and deliverables across cross-functional teams.

Drive continuous improvement by evaluating workflows, identifying root causes, and implementing scalable solutions.

**4. Technology Partnership and Prioritizatio**n

Serve as the liaison between Quality Operations and the Technology and Product teams, translating operational needs into clearly defined business requirements, use cases, and success measures.

Lead prioritization of quality-related technology requests and enhancements based on quality impact, operational risk, and timing; maintain a transparent backlog and roadmap in partnership with Technology.

Track delivery of technology work against committed timelines, coordinate user acceptance testing and rollout with operations and market users, and escalate risks or delays as needed.

**5. Health Plan Partnershi**p

Work alongside the Payor team to track, manage, and follow up on open health plan items, requests, and deliverables, ensuring clear ownership and timely resolution.

Attend and actively participate in health plan meetings, including Joint Operating Committees (JOCs) and quality working sessions, to build strong partnerships with health plan partners and drive quality results.

Lead operational discussions with health plans on quality programs, data exchange and supplemental data, gap closure, and quality results; ensure action items from health plan meetings are documented and completed.

Maintain a consolidated view of health plan quality commitments, programs, and incentive opportunities across markets to inform prioritization and resource planning.

**6. Stakeholder and Vendor Managemen**t

Build collaborative relationships with Regional Quality, Market, Payor, Clinical, Analytics, Coding, Risk Adjustment, Technology, Product, Finance, and other enterprise partners.

Lead operational discussions with vendors and external partners; monitor results against service levels, quality standards, and contractual commitments.

Support materials and deliverables for executive, Board, JOC, CQC, and other governance forums as requested.

**Other Job Functions:**

* Understand, adhere to, and implement the Company’s policies and procedures.
* Provide leadership, coaching, and mentoring to employees and team members.
* Support hiring, employee reviews, workforce planning, and development activities for the function.
* Demonstrate excellent communication, customer service, attention to detail, and accountability.
* Travel as required.
* Other duties as assigned.

**Required Qualifications:**

**Minimum Experience**

* Minimum of 9 years of applicable healthcare quality, clinical operations, or program operations experience, including at least 3 years of people management experience.
* Demonstrated experience leading complex, cross-functional quality programs in Medicare Advantage, value-based care, HEDIS/Stars, ACO/MSSP, or a comparable environment.
* Experience overseeing large-scale operational programs, vendors, KPI tracking, and process improvement; IHA or in-home clinical program experience strongly preferred.
* Strong working knowledge of Stars, HEDIS, CAHPS, CMS and NCQA requirements, quality measurement, and healthcare operations.
* Proven track record as a strong, hands-on operator who drives execution, holds teams and partners accountable, and delivers results in a fast-paced, matrixed environment.
* Experience partnering directly with health plans (e.g., JOCs, quality program partnerships) and with technology teams on requirements and prioritization strongly preferred.

**2. Education/Licensure:**

Bachelor’s degree required in healthcare administration, public health, nursing, business, data analytics, or a related field; advanced degree preferred

**Skills and Abilities**:

1. Strong operator with a bias for action; able to take ambiguous problems, build a plan, and drive them to completion

2. Ability to manage multiple priorities, workstreams, and deadlines simultaneously with minimal supervision

3. Skilled at influencing and aligning cross-functional, regional, market, and external stakeholders without direct authority

4. Ability to translate operational needs into clear technology requirements and priorities

5. Excellent analytical, problem-solving, and organizational skills; uses data to monitor results and drive decisions

6. Exceptional attention to detail and follow-through; ensures open items are tracked and closed

7. Language Skills: Strong communication skills both written and verbal to work with multiple internal and external clients in a fast-paced environment

8. Mathematical Skills: Ability to work with mathematical concepts such as probability and statistical inference. Ability to apply concepts such as fractions, percentages, ratios, and proportions to practical situations.

9. Reasoning Ability: Ability to apply principles of logical or scientific thinking to a wide range of intellectual and practical problems.

10. Computer Skills: Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint); experience with project and work management tools preferred

**Essential Physical Functions**:

These are requirements normally expected to perform regular job duties. Incumbent must be able to successfully perform all the functions of the job with or without accommodation.

  
  
  
  

**Location****:**
=================

Remote - GA

**Pay Range****:**
==================

$129,700.00 - $162,100.00

Salary range shown is a guideline. Individual compensation packages can vary based on factors unique to each candidate, such as skill set, experience, and qualifications.

existing_roles.description:
Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit www.shield.ai. Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn, X, Instagram, and YouTube.

### **About Shield AI:**

Shield AI is a venture-backed defense technology company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Our products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies.

### **Job Description:**

We’re looking for a hands-on quality leader to take X-BAT from early prototype builds through production launch and into rate production.

You will build the aircraft quality organization and establish the quality capability for our new Seattle-area production facility, X-Forge 3. You’ll own product and process quality across prototype, pre-series and production builds, ensuring that lessons from development become effective controls as the program scales.

This role owns the Quality Management System, quality engineering, inspection, nonconformance management and audit readiness for the X-BAT manufacturing operation. You’ll partner with Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Production and Supply Chain to prevent defects, resolve recurring problems and deliver aircraft that meet technical, customer and applicable regulatory requirements.

We need a technically credible leader who can build practical, scalable systems, make sound decisions under schedule pressure and challenge senior stakeholders constructively while keeping execution moving.

**What you'll do:**

* **Build quality into prototype and launch**

  + Lead quality planning and execution for X-BAT prototype and development builds, establishing appropriate inspection, test evidence and build records as designs evolve.
  + Partner with Engineering and Manufacturing Engineering to identify product and process risks, define critical controls and build quality requirements into tooling, work instructions and test plans.
  + Establish configuration and traceability controls with Engineering and Production, ensuring each aircraft’s build status, deviations and nonconformances are understood and documented.
  + Capture lessons from build, integration and test issues, and drive their incorporation into design changes, manufacturing processes and future builds.
  + Define quality readiness criteria for pre-series builds and production launch, validating inspection methods, process controls, workforce competence and closure of significant risks.

  **Establish the Seattle quality operation**

  + Recruit, develop and lead the quality team, building the technical capability and frontline support needed as aircraft production grows.
  + Establish and maintain a lean, effective QMS for X-Forge 3, aligned with Shield AI’s wider quality framework, AS9100, ISO 9001 and applicable customer requirements.
  + Lead certification readiness and internal, customer and external audits, driving timely closure and sustained effectiveness of corrective actions.
  + Set up receiving, in-process and final inspection capability, including measurement equipment, calibration, training and quality records, in partnership with relevant functions.

  **Deliver quality at rate**

  + Own production quality performance, using first-pass yield, defects, rework and escapes to focus action where it improves aircraft quality and production flow.
  + Lead containment, root cause analysis and corrective action for manufacturing quality issues, with clear functional ownership and verification that fixes prevent recurrence.
  + Own the nonconformance and MRB process, ensuring disposition decisions follow approved technical authority and that affected hardware remains controlled.
  + Partner with Supply Chain and supplier quality teams to resolve incoming quality issues and improve supplier performance before defects disrupt aircraft builds.
  + Work with Engineering and Production to define acceptance evidence and ensure aircraft meet approved requirements before release.
  + Use digital quality tools and manufacturing data to strengthen traceability, expose trends and reduce manual administration as production scales.
  + Give leadership a clear view of quality performance, product risks and readiness; escalate or stop affected work when requirements or product integrity cannot be assured.

**Required qualifications:**

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering, quality or a related technical field.
* 10+ years of leadership experience in quality, product assurance or reliability within aerospace, defense technology or high-reliability manufacturing.
* Demonstrated success leading quality through prototype or new product introduction and into sustained production.
* Proven ability to build and scale quality teams and systems while supporting fast-paced development and manufacturing operations.
* Deep expertise in containment, root cause analysis, MRB, corrective and preventive action, and continuous improvement.
* Strong working knowledge of AS9100 and ISO 9001, with practical implementation and audit leadership experience.
* Experience with complex assembly, inspection, configuration control, traceability and product acceptance.
* Ability to influence and challenge senior leaders constructively across Engineering, Production and Supply Chain.
* A hands-on leadership style and sound technical judgment, balancing timely execution with clear quality standards and accountability.

**Preferred qualifications:**

* Direct experience taking a new aircraft program from prototype through production launch and rate ramp.
* Experience establishing quality capability at a new manufacturing facility or transferring production between sites.
* Experience in aircraft final assembly, systems integration, production test and reliability improvement.
* Experience deploying digital quality systems, statistical process controls and data-driven defect prevention.
* Advanced degree in engineering, quality or a related technical discipline.

#LF

Pay within range listed + Bonus + Benefits + Equity

Temporary employee offer package:

Pay within range listed above + temporary benefits package (applicable after 60 days of employment)

Salary compensation is influenced by a wide array of factors including but not limited to skill set, level of experience, licenses and certifications, and specific work location. All offers are contingent on a cleared background and possible reference check. Military fellows and part-time employees are not eligible for benefits. Please speak to your talent acquisition representative for more information.

###

Shield AI is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace and is an affirmative action employer. We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender identity or Veteran status. If you have a disability or special need that requires accommodation, please let us know.

existing_roles.description:
**JOB TITLE: Head of Front-End Sales, America's, Energy and Infrastructure Projects**

**LOCATION: Raleigh, NC (Hybrid)**

**Who we are?**

Built on more than a century of innovation and decades of substation expertise, **Linxon** blends AtkinsRéalis' project management strength with Hitachi Energy's technological leadership. Together, we deliver high‑performing EPC solutions that strengthen the power grid.

We support community growth and industrial development by providing end‑to‑end engineering, procurement, management, and construction services for complex AC substation and electrification projects across five core markets.

**What We Believe?**

We believe in the value of every client's'investment and take pride in tackling challenging, high‑risk projects. With deep expertise and continuous development, our teams operate with the precision, resilience, and mission‑focus needed to deliver crucial infrastructure—often described as the "special forces" of our industry.

To learn more about us click on the link below:

Careers - Linxon

  

**How will you make your impact?**

As the **Head of Quality,** you will leader to define, implement, and continuously improve the Quality Management System across the Americas. This role is responsible for ensuring quality is designed into every stage of project delivery, from engineering and procurement through construction, commissioning, and closeout. This is a highly visible leadership role with direct influence on project performance, supplier quality, operational discipline, customer satisfaction, and continuous improvement across the Americas.

The **Head of Quality** will establish and lead a quality organization that embeds quality into how projects are planned, executed, and continuously improved.

You will drive a preventive approach to quality by strengthening planning, supplier oversight, project controls, auditing, and lessons learned. You will create the frameworks that connect Engineering, Procurement, Construction, Project Delivery, and Quality into a single system focused on delivering projects right the first time. Success will be measured by reductions in rework and recurring issues, stronger supplier performance, improved audit outcomes, increased first-time-right execution, and the maturity of the quality culture across the organization.

**What will you do?**

  

* You will lead the development and continuous improvement of the Americas Quality Management System (QMS), ensuring consistent standards, governance, and accountability across the region.
* You will establish quality requirements and controls from tender through project closeout to ensure quality is built into project delivery from the outset.
* You will implement risk-based supplier qualification, surveillance, inspection, and release processes to improve supplier quality performance.
* You will ensure inspection and test plans align with engineering requirements, contract obligations, and construction execution strategies.
* You will lead audits, management reviews, quality assurance programs, and performance reporting across the project portfolio.
* You will drive root-cause analysis and corrective action processes that address systemic issues rather than isolated events.
* You will establish and lead continuous improvement initiatives focused on reducing defects, rework, and the Cost of Poor Quality.
* You will build and develop a high-performing Quality Assurance and Quality Control organization across the Americas.
* You will strengthen collaboration across Engineering, Procurement, PMO, Construction, and HSE to improve quality outcomes throughout the project lifecycle.
* You will develop quality capability, training programs, succession plans, and best practices that support long-term organizational growth.
* You will assess and strengthen the Americas Quality Management System, focusing resources on the highest-priority risks and improvement opportunities.
* You will establish clear quality governance, accountability, and performance reporting across the region.
* You will standardize project quality planning, supplier quality management, inspection requirements, and NCR governance practices.
* You will improve visibility into the Cost of Poor Quality, quality trends, and leading indicators across the project portfolio.
* You will reduce recurring quality issues, rework, and warranty exposure through stronger preventive controls and root-cause resolution.
* You will improve audit performance, supplier quality outcomes, and project readiness before execution begins.
* You will create a culture where quality is proactively planned, owned, measured, and continuously improved across functions.
* You will build a scalable quality organization capable of supporting Linxon's continued growth across the Americas.

**Who you are?**

  

* You are an experienced quality leader with 7-15+ years of experience in EPC, power, industrial, construction, manufacturing, or other complex project environments.
* You are proven in leading multi-project or regional Quality Management Systems and driving quality performance across diverse operations.
* You are knowledgeable in ISO 9001 principles, supplier quality management, project QA/QC, auditing practices, and root-cause methodologies.
* You are skilled at translating quality data and performance trends into preventive actions, operational discipline, and business improvements.
* You are experienced in developing quality organizations, improving governance, and building sustainable quality cultures.
* You hold a degree in engineering, quality, or a related technical field, and quality or auditing certifications are considered an asset.
* You are a leader who puts the mission, the customer, and the team ahead of individual recognition.
* You are comfortable making decisions with incomplete information and adjusting course as conditions change.
* You are committed to raising standards while fostering respect, inclusion, and psychological safety.
* You are passionate about developing people, sharing knowledge, and strengthening organizational capability.
* You are trusted because of your actions, credibility, and follow-through rather than your title.
* You are disciplined, data-driven, and focused on creating systems that prevent issues rather than simply react to them.

The US base salary range for this full-time position is $136,300 to $261,200. Our salary ranges are determined by role, level, and location. Within the range, individual pay is determined by work location and additional factors, including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training. Your recruiter can share more about the specific salary range for your preferred location during the hiring process.

Please note that the compensation details listed in US role postings reflect the base salary only, and do not include bonus, equity, or benefits.

**What We Offer:**

* **Competitive Salary:** Enjoy a rewarding compensation package that reflects your contributions.
* **Health, Dental, and Vision Coverage:** Comprehensive benefits to support your well-being and that of your family.
* **401K with Employer Match** : Invest in your future with our generous retirement savings plan.
* **Employee Assistance Program (EAP)**: Access confidential support for personal and professional challenges.
* **Paid Time Off (PTO):** Recharge and relax with ample time off to maintain work-life balance.
* **Learning and Development:** Expand your skills through training programs and career-building opportunities.
* **Mentorship Initiatives:** Connect with experienced professionals for guidance, support, and career insight.
* **Internal Mobility:** Explore opportunities across departments and office locations to broaden your experience.
* **Performance-Based Advancement:** Grow your career through clear pathways tied to your achievements and impact.

We are proud to announce that **LinxonAmericas** has been certified as a **Great Place to Work®** reflecting our commitment to fostering a diverse, inclusive environment that fuels innovation and teamwork.

**#Linxon**

* Coordinate the preparation of technical reports, publications, and oral presentations

existing_roles.description:
Kentucky Trailer

As a part of the global industrial organization Marmon Holdings—which is backed by Berkshire Hathaway—you’ll be doing things that matter, leading at every level, and winning a better way. We’re committed to making a positive impact on the world, providing you with diverse learning and working opportunities, and fostering a culture where everyone’s empowered to be their best.

Job Title: Director of Operations
  
Division: Kentucky Trailer  
Location: Louisville, KY- 3 site locations  
Reports to: President, Kentucky Trailer  
FLSA: Exempt  
  
This position has multiple direct reports across 3 sites. Current direct reports include Operations Manager, 7 Team Leaders, and a Manufacturing Engineer/Facilities Manager. This position requires local travel between the 3 sites in Louisville.  
  
Kentucky Trailer has been building in Louisville since 1879, when it was founded as the Kentucky Wagon Manufacturing Company. Today it designs and builds custom trailers and truck bodies for moving and storage, snack food distribution, package delivery, and specialty markets such as mobile medical, government, and motorsports. Most of what we build is engineered to order rather than off the shelf, which makes our operations both challenging and rewarding to lead.  
  
The Director of Operations leads all day-to-day manufacturing operations and is accountable for Safety, Quality, Delivery, Cost, People, and Productivity results. The role owns the manufacturing operating budget, develops frontline leaders, and builds a culture of accountability and continuous improvement. Works closely with Materials, Supply Chain, Engineering, Finance, Human Resources, and Commercial Sales to make sure production plans are executable and customer commitments are met. The workforce is non-union.

**Position Key Accountabilities:**

### **Safety**

* Create and sustain a Safety First and Always culture, with every employee understanding their personal responsibility for a safe workplace.
* Enforce safety policies, procedures and safe work practices at every level of the organization.
* Make sure hazards, near misses and incidents are addressed promptly, with root causes corrected.
* Ensure compliance with OSHA and environmental requirements and lead continuous improvement toward an incident-free workplace.

### **Manufacturing performance and planning**

* Lead daily manufacturing activities to meet production schedules and customer delivery commitments.
* Set clear daily, weekly and monthly expectations for each production area, and align labor and resources to requirements.
* Identify production constraints and implement corrective actions to improve throughput.
* Partner with Supply Chain and Materials so schedules are executable and escalate shortages before they affect production.
* Support point-of-use inventory, Kanban, vendor-managed inventory and other Lean material strategies where appropriate.

### **Quality**

* Build a culture where quality is owned at the point of manufacture and the next operation is treated as the customer.
* Ensure compliance with manufacturing standards, specifications, work instructions and quality procedures.
* Partner with Engineering to drive root-cause corrective action and reduce defects, rework, warranty exposure and cost of poor quality.

### **Lean and operational excellence**

* Champion Lean Manufacturing using 5S, Standard Work, Visual Management, Kaizen and structured problem solving.
* Establish a disciplined management cadence of daily production meetings, visual boards, KPI reviews and structured follow-up.
* Ensure standard work is documented, followed and continuously improved.
* Drive measurable improvement in labor productivity, cycle time, throughput, material flow, space utilization and manufacturing cost.
* Lead automation and capital initiatives that improve safety, quality, productivity and cost.

### **Financial performance and cost**

* Own the manufacturing operating budget and take part in the annual budget and monthly forecasts.
* Manage to labor, overhead and operating cost targets, including direct labor productivity, overtime and indirect labor.
* Ensure accuracy in both labor reporting and BOM usages
* WIP accuracy, and operational support for cycle counts and physical inventories.
* Partner with Finance to analyze manufacturing variances and carry out corrective actions.
* Prepare ROI justifications for capital requests and track whether completed projects deliver the promised return.

### **Maintenance and facilities**

* Ensure preventive maintenance programs maximize equipment uptime and extend asset life.
* Improve utilization of equipment, facilities and manufacturing capacity.

### **Leadership and people development**

* Lead, coach and develop managers, team leaders and employees across the operation.
* Set annual performance goals and development plans and hold leaders accountable for results.
* Build frontline leaders' capability in problem solving, waste elimination and employee accountability.
* Build organizational depth through hiring, succession planning and cross-training.
* Communicate regularly with employees about performance, company expectations, policies and priorities.

**Requirements**
----------------

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering, Manufacturing or another technical discipline, or equivalent experience.
* Minimum 10 years in manufacturing with a proven record of success and increasing responsibility.
* Minimum 5 years leading multi-site operations through managers and leaders.
* Demonstrated record of improving safety performance
* Lean Manufacturing experience or certification, with measurable results in efficiency improvement and cost reduction.
* Demonstrated P&L or operating budget accountability.
* Experience with ERP/MRP systems.
* Excellent written and verbal communication and problem-solving skills.
* Ability to manage multiple projects and priorities at once.
* Willingness to live and work in the greater Louisville, KY area.

**Preferred qualifications**
----------------------------

* Trailer, truck body or similar fabrication, welding and assembly experience.
* Experience in high-mix, custom build-to-order manufacturing.
* MBA or other financial education.

**Working conditions**
----------------------

This role works in both office and manufacturing plant settings, with exposure to noise, welding, painting and moving equipment. Required PPE must be worn on the production floor. The role regularly requires walking and standing for extended periods.

Employment is contingent on successful completion of a background check and drug screen.

Following receipt of a conditional offer of employment, candidates will be required to complete additional job-related screening processes as permitted or required by applicable law.

We are an equal opportunity employer, and all applicants will be considered for employment without attention to their membership in any protected class. If you require any reasonable accommodation to complete your application or any part of the recruiting process, please email your request to careers@marmon.com, and please be sure to include the title and the location of the position for which you are applying.

Why LeoLabs?

At LeoLabs, we're building the living map of activity in space. Through our proprietary global radar network and AI-enabled analytics platform, we collect millions of measurements daily on more than 25,000 objects in low Earth orbit (LEO). Our radar-powered intelligence protects billions in assets, monitors adversarial behavior, and ensures safe operations for commercial and government missions.

We're not just building technology, we are redefining global security, safety, and transparency in space. As orbital activity accelerates and threats grow more complex, LeoLabs is a trusted partner for Space Domain Awareness, Space Traffic Management, and Satellite Operations for top-tier space operators and allied defense organizations.

If you're looking to work on mission-critical challenges at the forefront of aerospace, national security, and AI, your impact starts here.

LeoLabs is seeking a Head of Manufacturing to lead the next phase of production scaling of our radar systems. This leader will own the manufacturing strategy, industrialization roadmap, quality management, facility scaling, and cross-functional execution required to increase production capacity beyond 10x. This role may be leveled as Senior Director or Vice President level based on the successful candidate’s experience, leadership scope and demonstrated ability to own the function. The role with report directly to the SVP, Radars. This role is a full-time, in-person position based at our headquarters in Menlo Park, CA. Regular domestic travel is expected.

The Head of Manufacturing will turn LeoLabs’ advanced radar designs from low/medium-rate initial production into repeatable, scalable, high-rate production systems. You will collaborate with and leverage support from Product, Supply Chain, Radar Systems and Hardware Engineering, Program Management, Finance and Accounting, and executive leadership to build the manufacturing capacity that enables LeoLabs to deploy radar systems more reliably and at greater scale for the U.S. Government, allies, and commercial customers.

The preferred candidate has done this before – they are a leader who has built and sustained a manufacturing system, rather than someone who has only managed an existing operation. This candidate is a hands-on manufacturing executive or emerging executive from a high-performance production environment such as aerospace, defense technology, automotive, or other complex hardware industries. They have scaled production systems from the ground up, built functional teams, improved quality, stood up facilities or production lines, and operated with urgency in environments where reliability, repeatability, and mission success matter.

Key Responsibilities

Manufacturing Strategy & Scale

* Own LeoLabs’ high-rate manufacturing and industrialization strategy for radar systems, subsystems, and associated high-reliability hardware across manufacturing, assembly, integration, and test operations.
* Build and scale a production system and team capable of supporting 10x growth in radar production over the next 2 years while maintaining high standards for quality, reliability, integration, and deployment readiness.
* Define the operating model across internal manufacturing, external suppliers, contract manufacturing, and integration partners.
* Own the high-rate production footprint plan including facility needs, equipment, tooling, staffing, and capital investment.
* Stand up scalable production lines, work cells, fixtures, test stations, documentation, and acceptance processes for radar hardware, RF systems, electronics, electromechanical assemblies, power systems, compute infrastructure, and system-level integration.
* Establish the scaled manufacturing steady state including production planning, throughput management, capacity planning, cost analysis, quality, and delivery execution.

Industrialization

* Own the transition from engineering builds to production-ready designs.
* Establish and mature release and readiness gates, first-article processes, and build documentation.
* Partner with Radar Systems and Hardware Engineering teams to industrialize new radar designs, ensuring manufacturability, testability, serviceability, configuration control, and production readiness.
* Partner with engineering NPI manufacturing team to improve manufacturability, DfX, and cost reduction opportunities.
* Ensure new radar products have validated build plans, test procedures, tooling, factory acceptance testing criteria, and supplier plans before production ramp.
* Create a functioning feedback system from manufacturing and sustainment back into product and engineering.

Quality, Reliability & Production

* Build and mature the quality management system required for high-reliability radar systems serving mission-critical customers.
* Establish clear standards for configuration control, traceability, inspection, nonconformance management, corrective action, supplier quality, and production acceptance.
* Drive measurable improvements in yield, first-pass quality, rework, scrap, field defects, and schedule performance.
* Build strong review mechanisms for failures, escapes, production risks, and systemic issues.
* Partner with Technical Program Management to align production readiness and execution with program, contract, customer, and deployment commitments
* Partner with Supply Chain on supplier readiness, long-lead planning, cost reduction, and risk mitigation.
* Partner with the Radar Operations Center and Global Infrastructure to turn field performance and maintenance data into product and process improvements to increase performance, reduce operational impacts, and decrease maintenance costs.
* Develop manufacturing KPIs and high-level dashboards for throughput, schedule metrics, yield, labor tracking, cost, quality, rework, scrap, supplier performance, and field reliability.

Team Leadership

* Establish and lead the LeoLabs Production System, creating a common operating model for safety, quality, delivery, cost and people. Implement tiered daily management, visual controls, standard work, structured problem solving, leader standard work, production flow, capacity management and continuous improvement.
* Recruit, develop, and lead a world-class manufacturing organization including manufacturing operations, production, test operations, quality, facilities, and related functions.
* Set clear ownership and metrics across the manufacturing organization.
* Build a culture of execution, urgency, accountability, safety, quality, and continuous improvement.

Required Qualifications

* 15+ years of experience in manufacturing, production operations, industrialization, factory operations, manufacturing engineering, or related operational leadership roles.
* Demonstrated experience implementing and leading a mature Lean manufacturing or production operating system, such as the Toyota Production System, including standard work, visual management, daily accountability, structured problem solving, flow, built-in quality, waste reduction and continuous improvement.
* Demonstrated experience scaling production capacity, standing up production lines or facilities, and improving throughput, quality, cost, and delivery performance.
* Experience manufacturing complex, high-reliability hardware in industries such as aerospace, defense, automotive, advanced electronics, robotics, industrial automation, energy systems, RF systems, communications, space systems, or mission-critical infrastructure.
* Experience with quality management systems and standards such as AS9100, ISO 9001, IPC standards, ESD controls, supplier quality, first-article inspection
* Strong technical fluency with hardware product development, NPI, configuration control, test operations, production readiness, and root-cause corrective action.
* Excellent communication, leadership, organizational, and stakeholder management skills.
* Eligibility to obtain and maintain required U.S. security clearances, as applicable to this role.
* Bachelor’s degree in engineering, manufacturing, operations, industrial engineering, supply chain, business, or a related discipline, or equivalent experience.

Preferred Qualifications

* Formal training or demonstrated practitioner experience in Toyota Production System, Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, Lean Six Sigma or an equivalent operating system. Black Belt, Master Black Belt, TPS practitioner/trainer or comparable credentials preferred.
* Experience developing greenfield or brownfield production facilities, production lines, integration sites, or manufacturing cells.
* Experience with radar, RF systems, antennas, communications systems, sensors, satellites, ground systems, aerospace systems, or other complex electromechanical products.
* Experience supporting Department of War, Space Force, NASA, or allied government customers.
* Experience working with classified, export-controlled, ITAR/EAR-controlled, or otherwise sensitive hardware programs.
* Master’s degree in engineering, operations, business administration, manufacturing, supply chain, or a related discipline.

Compensation

This position is benchmarked to San Francisco Bay Area with a base salary range of $225,000 - $248,000, plus bonus, equity, and benefits.

Compensation Note: The salary range for this position is benchmarked based on the designated primary work location for the role. Final compensation may vary depending on the selected candidate’s work location, applicable market data, experience, qualifications, and other job-related factors.

Perks and Benefits
